cap.p.name.name: Name your publisher
cap.p.name.note: Not "publisher_id" or "domain." A real human name the recipient will recognise on the trust prompt later.
cap.p.server.name: Add a server
cap.p.server.note: Auto-detect when the user has the Daal CLI running on the VPS. Otherwise, paste an endpoint or postpone — never block onboarding.
cap.p.share.name: Share with family
cap.p.share.note: QR + PIN + 6-word fingerprint, all visible at once. The publisher reads the words on a phone call so the recipient can verify the trust prompt — the same six words appear on their device.
cap.p.welcome.name: What is publishing?
cap.p.welcome.note: Same three-card pattern as recipient, but the accent shifts from gold to a muted cyan so power-users know where they are.
cap.r.pin.name: Set a PIN
cap.r.pin.note: Honest copy on the trade-off. "Skip" is not buried — many users on shared phones won't want a PIN.
cap.r.ready.name: Ready to connect
cap.r.ready.note: The flourish: the shield button breathes a soft gold halo. The selected route is shown as a chip — never the raw ID.
cap.r.route.name: Add a route
cap.r.route.note: Four equal tiles. The "Recommended" flag on subscribe is the only nudge — every option is real and reachable.
cap.r.what.name: What is Daal?
cap.r.what.note: Three claims, no jargon. The italic Roman numerals are a quiet editorial cue, not a feature list.
cap.welcome.name: Welcome
cap.welcome.note: Logo, tagline, language toggle. The only screen with the wordmark at full scale.
cap.who.name: Who are you?
cap.who.note: The branch. Recipient and publisher are equally weighted — neither is "the default." "Not sure yet" routes to recipient with a banner that lets the user switch.
foot.p: From here, both users land on the main app's Connection screen. The recipient sees the phoenix glowing, one tap from connected. The publisher sees a small "publisher dashboard" entry alongside, where they can manage subscribers, rotate keys, and watch route health.
foot.p2: The branching choice is reversible: Settings → Advanced → "I am a publisher" toggles the publisher surface on for any user who started as a recipient.
hero.lede: People inside Iran land on the recipient flow — get a route, press connect. Diaspora who want to help family land on the publisher flow — set up a server, share a subscription with the people they love. Both paths leave first-launch ready.
lane.publisher.sub: For diaspora setting up a VPS to make routes for family back home. Same warmth, slightly more capable surface — marked with a quiet teal-cyan accent so power users know they're in publisher mode.
lane.publisher.title: Publisher · "I want to help others"
lane.recipient.sub: For people inside Iran on shaky networks. The path optimises for one outcome: at the end, the phoenix is glowing and the user is one tap away from a working connection.
lane.recipient.title: Recipient · "I want to connect"
lane.shared.sub: Everyone sees these two screens. The branching choice on screen two decides which path the rest of onboarding takes.
lane.shared.title: Shared start
p.name.hint: You can change this later. Keep it personal — your people will recognise it.
p.name.label: Display name
p.name.sub: This is what your family will see when they subscribe — not a URL, just a friendly name.
p.name.title: Name your publisher.
p.server.label: Server endpoint
p.server.later: I'll set up later — show me the dashboard
p.server.sub: Add the VPS or server you've already set up. Daal generates signed routes from it — your provider never knows about Daal.
p.server.title: Where will routes run from?
p.share.fp: Your fingerprint — read these aloud to verify
p.share.title: Share with your people.
p.welcome.c1.p: Subscribers verify your fingerprint once. They trust the publisher, not the network.
p.welcome.c2.p: There is no Daal server. Your subscription URL goes peer-to-peer, or through whatever channel you choose.
p.welcome.sub: You'll create routes that family and friends can subscribe to. Your server, your keys, your trusted circle — Daal does not see any of it.
p.welcome.title: Welcome, publisher.
r.pin.sub: A PIN protects your routes if someone takes your phone. You'll enter it each time you open Daal.
r.pin.title: Protect your routes.
r.ready.p: First connect asks for VPN permission once.
r.ready.title: Ready when you are.
r.route.sub: Pick whichever you have. You can add more later.
r.route.t1.p: Paste a daal:// link or scan a QR.
r.route.title: Add your first route.
r.what.c1.p: Daal helps you reach the open internet when your country blocks it.
r.what.c2.p: A route is the path your traffic takes. You can get them from a publisher, a friend, or a file.
r.what.c3.p: They live on this device. Daal does not see your traffic, and we do not run a server.
r.what.title: What is Daal?
who.publisher.p: I run a server abroad. I want to make routes for my family and friends back home.
who.recipient.p: I'm looking for a way to reach the open internet. I have a route from a friend or publisher — or I'm looking for one.
who.sub: Daal works two ways. Pick the one that sounds like you — you can change it later.
who.title: Who are you?
